feeds.title: Mr. Money Mustache Blog
feeds.description: Mr. Money Mustache is a 30 something retiree who now writes about how we can all lead a frugal yet Badass life of leisure. I decided to start this blog to share some of the secrets of how all this can be done. How you can create a life that is better than your current one, that just happens to cost 50-75% less.

feeds.title: Aussie Firebug Blog
feeds.description: Aussie Firebug is an anonymous blog detailing the journey to financial independence through investing in real estate, low-cost index funds, and Super. By investing at a young age and consistently it is possible to reach a point where your investments pay you enough money to live off forever.

feeds.title: Physician On FIRE Blog
feeds.description: Physician on FIRE is a personal finance website devoted to helping high-income professionals achieve financial independence and the option to retire early.

feeds.title: Retire by 40
feeds.description: Posts on early retirement, frugal lifestyle, making money, real estate and stocks. Joe Udo wants to change the way you think about retirement. Retire by 40 is a place to share his aspiration for Financial Independence.

feeds.title: Early Retirement Now
feeds.description: Here you will find post on Personal finance fans, saving for early retirement in 2018. DIY frugal financial planners and turbo-savers.

feeds.title: Go Curry Cracker
feeds.description: Through the power of travel hacking, tax minimization, geographic arbitrage, medical tourism, and financial independence through aggressive saving, Winnie and Jeremy aspires to help others to do the same. It includes blogs, forums, and recommendations. They have been retired in 30s to travel the world and start a family.

feeds.title: Mad Fientist
feeds.description: Mad Fientist is a blog dedicated to achieving early financial independence, and includes strategies and for pursuing financial independence and early retirement.

feeds.title: Millennial Revolution
feeds.description: Welcome to the Millennial Revolution, a FIRE (Financial Independence Retire Early) site started by two computer engineers/children's authors, FIRECracker & Wanderer, who retired at 31 to travel the world! Check out our blog for the latest writings, strategies, current updates, and more.

feeds.title: 1500 Days to Freedom
feeds.description: 1500 Days is a blog about my journey to early retirement in 1500 days, or approximately 4 years. I am not giving financial advice, but sharing with you various ways I save money to enable retirement in my early 40s.

feeds.title: Tawcan
feeds.description: Hi, I'm Bob Lai from Vancouver Canada. Tawcan.com is Canadian personal finance and dividend investing blog dedicated to chronicle my quest for joyful life and financial independence. My wife & I started our financial independence & retire early journey in 2011 after a financial epiphany. By investing in US & Canadian dividend stocks, we are aiming to achieve financial independence in our 40's & living off dividends.

feeds.title: A Purple Life
feeds.description: Hi! In 2015 I started this blog and hatched a plan to retire in 10 years at 35. With the help of decreased spending, increased wages, and geo arbitrage. I reached my goal in half the time and retired in 2020 at age 30. This blog catalogs my journey to and through early retirement.

feeds.title: Route To Retire
feeds.description: Hi, I'm Jim - I'm just a regular guy who figured out the path to financial freedom and early retirement for myself & my family. We reached financial independence and I retired from my corporate job at the end of 2018 at the age of 43. Join me on our journey as I talk about what I've learned so far and as we figure out ways to optimize our strategy.

feeds.title: Accidentally Retired
feeds.description: Accidentally Retired is my journey from being a CEO to finding myself accidentally retired at the age of 36. I never intended to retire early (though I may have fantasized about it), but Accidentally Retired is my exploration of Financial Independence, Early Retirement, Enjoying Life and more.

feeds.title: The Wealthy Accountant » Early Retirement
feeds.description: By the time I was 22 I retired. Sounds insane, but it is true. I bought a home and a beater car and a Huffy bike. I spent my days reading, learning, hiking, biking and taking a few classes at the local college. I still prepared around 50 tax returns each spring. I love my clients so I did it. Here I Share my experience to help you reach your dreams, too.

feeds.title: TicTocLife
feeds.description: Our story of going from full-time careers at 35 to early retirement and financial independence.

feeds.title: MoneyMow Blog
feeds.description: Writing about financial independence and early retirement while documenting my journey towards retiring early in seven years at age 33.

feeds.title: Abandoned Cubicle
feeds.description: Welcome to abandoned cubicle, where I write about the race to early retirement, personal finance, cubicle job survival, its merits, and its pitfalls. Follow along and find yourself some inspiration, save a few bucks, and focus on what's truly important in life.

feeds.title: My Journey To Financial Independence
feeds.description: A journey to financial independence from the very beginning. My personal investments are designed to maximize for sleeping well at night, not necessarily scouting for the highest returns.

feeds.title: Dad is FIRE
feeds.description: Greg shares his journey to and through early retirement, and retiring early. Also covers articles about personal finance, financial independence and real estate.

feeds.title: Early Retirement Earl
feeds.description: Earlyretirementearl.com is where I share all the tips and tricks that I used personally to help me achieve financial independence and retire early.

feeds.title: My Road to FIRE Blog
feeds.description: Hello! Welcome to Road to FIRE. This is where you'll read about my journey to financial independence. Along the way, I will share my learnings, struggles, failures, and wins. And periodically I will be featuring friends who are also on this journey.

feeds.title: Incoming Assets
feeds.description: We are Steph and Cel - a couple in our thirties, living in Vancouver, Canada. Inspired by some of our favourite money bloggers we decided to chronicle our own journey towards early retirement. Our goal is to be financially independent, meaning earning enough money through passive index investing to easily cover all expenses, by age 35.

feeds.title: Two Sides of FI
feeds.description: Two lifelong friends document and share their personal journey as they seek to become financially independent and retire early.

feeds.title: The Retirement Manifesto
feeds.description: The Retirement Manifesto is a website focused on Helping Others Achieve A Great Retirement! My goal is to educate, challenge and encourage each of you to take the steps necessary to achieve success and financial independence on your journey toward retirement.

feeds.title: Budgets Are Sexy
feeds.description: The Budgets Are Sexy blog was started in Feb of 2008 by J. Money, a personal finance nerd. For me, the Budgets Are Sexy blog has always been about the community. Sharing cool ideas, sharing lessons learned, and making money is a FUN topic to talk about! I believe everyone's path to financial independence is slightly different, and I'm excited to share more about mine.

feeds.title: Accidental Fire
feeds.description: Hi, I'm Dave. I'm writing from the position of having already achieved wealth and financial independence, and I want to help you get there too. So dig in, I hope you find some useful musings. My intention is not to re-hash the basics of the FIRE lifestyle or journey. Others have already done a much better job of that than I'd ever do. I like to focus on the behaviors and lifestyle factors that drive money decisions.

feeds.title: Retire Before Dad
feeds.description: I'm a 46-year-old Dad and investor based in the Washington, DC area. My plan is to retire at age 55 (or earlier). To reach this goal, I invest in index funds and individual stocks in retirement accounts. I'm building multiple income streams to fund my early retirement through real estate crowdfunding, stock dividends, and side business income via this blog.

feeds.title: The Fioneers
feeds.description: Hi, we're Jess and Corey. We're the founders of The Fioneers, a financial independence blog that we started together in September 2018. We're on a journey to financial independence. Our goal is to prioritize living life to the fullest today while buying our freedom for the future.

feeds.title: Financial Samurai
feeds.description: Financial Samurai delves deeper into investing, real estate, retirement planning, and career strategies, to achieve financial independence sooner, rather than later. Every article is written based on firsthand experience to provide the most helpful insights possible. Financial Samurai is one of the largest independently-owned personal finance sites in the world.

feeds.title: Our Next Life
feeds.description: For those aspiring to retire early or achieve financial independence, as well as those who've already gotten there. The blog is written by Tanja Hester, author of Work Optional and Wallet Activism.

feeds.title: Can I Retire Yet?
feeds.description: Accelerate Your Retirement by getting the updates on health insurance, investing & taxes, lifestyle, real estate and retirement calculators and decisions. It is your retirement roadmap to save more, invest smarter, retire sooner. Darrow Kirkpatrick is focused on the personal finance needs of anyone who is thinking about retirement or early retirement. His goal is to serve as a trustworthy and independent resource for readers as they navigate one of modern life's most complex and expensive transitions: retirement.

feeds.title: Top Questions And Answers
feeds.description: Top Questions And Answers is your ultimate guide to achieving financial freedom and building wealth through effective personal finance strategies, investment advice, and passive income stream. We offer expert tips on early retirement planning, debt reduction, budgeting, saving money, and wealth management to help you achieve financial independence and secure your financial future

feeds.title: Financially Alert
feeds.description: Hello! Hi, my name is Michael Quan. I reached financial independence (F.I.) in my 30s and retired early (R.E.) from a traditional career when I was 36. This was made possible through a combination of aggressive saving & investing, entrepreneurship, and real estate. Now it's my turn to help others to become financially alert. This means openly sharing the knowledge, strategies, and beliefs that can fuel financial freedom for life.

feeds.title: Freedom 35 Blog
feeds.description: I'm Liquid. Freedom 35 was started in 2010 as a public diary to track my journey to becoming financially independent before I turn 35 years old. Recently, I became financially independent in 2020. Check out my Freedom 35 Blog as it features relevant news & insightful commentary on personal finance, investing, early retirement, and passive income creation.

feeds.title: Steve Adcock
feeds.description: Hi there, I'm Steve. I am an entrepreneur and writer. I retired from full-time work at 35 and now write, blog, and speak about no B.S. personal finance, financial freedom, and early retirement. If you are looking for the latest articles on how to build wealth, how to get rich & retire early, you've landed in the right place.

feeds.title: Retire In Progress Blog
feeds.description: I'm Giorgio, a 43 years old software engineer from Italy who lives in Switzerland since November 2012. In this blog, I discuss Switzerland-specific aspects of FIRE, real-time ultra-detailed Net Worth & Cash-Flow tracking, my storytelling skills, and more.

feeds.title: Money Flamingo Blog
feeds.description: Money Flamingo is a Financial Independence blog focusing on alternative paths to FIRE (like Coast FI and Flamingo FI). We are a married couple with two young kids and live in Sydney, Australia. We semi-retired in 2020 at 35 and 39 years old.

feeds.title: Tread Lightly, Retire Early
feeds.description: Hello, I'm Angela, a Pacific Northwest, mama to one awesome five-year-old son & have been married since I was just twenty-one. I work as a LEED AP for a company that builds green, affordable communities in urban areas. I have no plans to quit but am still very much focused on financial independence. Join me on my journey to tread lightly and (maybe) retire early.

feeds.title: Retire By 45 Blog
feeds.description: Get inspiration, tips & resources to help you retire by 45. Enjoy 20 more years of travel, adventure, recreation & time with friends and family.

feeds.title: Wealthy Healthy Life of Adventure
feeds.description: Personal Finance Adventure to Financial Freedom and Early Retirement. Welcome to my blog Wealthy Healthy Life. One day I'd like to write a book, so instead of talking about it, I'm getting on with it. I have started writing this blog on lessons learned, my first-hand experiences, and successes that I think are worthwhile sharing. I have had many interesting experiences in my life, good and bad, but always enjoyed life and luckily have a loving family.

feeds.title: I Retired Young
feeds.description: Hi! I'm David, from the UK, used to be an accountant. I decided to retire early and stopped working at the end of 2016 when I was 47. Since then I blog about my journey to financial freedom and my early retirement experience. Visit my blog to discover the steps I took to retire early at 47 with weekly posts about what I do to enjoy my early retirement & how much it costs.

feeds.title: theFIREstarter
feeds.description: Financial Independence and Early Retirement blog. Read about life hacks, money saving tips, frugal food, general views on life and of course the occasional rant.

feeds.title: Engineer Seeking FIRE Blog
feeds.description: I started thinking about this blog when I was talking to my wife and explaining the concept of FIRE (Financial Independence Retire Early). Since we're both engineers working in high-tech, we had been focusing on improving our job performance, in order to increase our income. However, in 2016 I learned about the FIRE movement and the focus on maximizing net worth. The goal was to have the option to retire early (which blew my mind, because everybody I knew was retiring around 60 years old).

feeds.title: Screw The Average Blog » FIRE
feeds.description: The following section of Screw The Average is dedicated to financial independence and early retirement aka FIRE. Our blog documents a journey of continual long-term travel, full-time house sitting, becoming digital nomads, pursuing financial independence, retire early (FI/RE). It's full of ideas, tips, and solutions. Join us on our journey, as over time we'll share our challenges, our stories, our goals, and our lessons learned.

feeds.title: Fire the Boss Blog
feeds.description: Hi, I'm Fraser, founder, and author of Fire The Boss. I created Fire The Boss to share my knowledge and entrepreneurial escapades, whilst guiding our readers (that's you!) towards financial freedom. I offer honest accounts; the good, the bad, and the ugly. This is a comprehensive personal finance resource and your guide to financial independence.

feeds.title: Millennial Money Honey
feeds.description: Hi, I'm Catie. Millennial Money Honey is a finance blog for single women working towards FIRE - financial independence retire early. Guided by the personal finance principles of Mr. Money Mustache, Quit Like A Millionaire, Vanguard's Jack Bogle, and more, their rules are decoded for everyone. Follow this graphic designer's money diary as she turns her index fund investments into financial freedom!

feeds.title: Rich Frugal Life
feeds.description: Hi! I'm Mrs. RFL. We're a family of 3 trying to live a rich frugal life on our way to financial independence and early retirement ('FIRE'). I retired in early 2020, at age 38, to help our family achieve the balance we desperately needed. Rich Frugal Life follows our FIRE journey and shares everything we learn (or screw up) along the way.

feeds.title: Millennial Money » Retire Early
feeds.description: Millennial Money shares their experience and lifestyle after Early Retirement in this segment of the blog. Hi, I'm Grant Sabatier. Making financial freedom accessible to all is my mission and passion. My passion is connecting and helping as many people as possible make smarter financial decisions, build more successful companies, reach financial independence, and live richer lives.

feeds.title: Canadian Dream: Free at 45
feeds.description: A blog about early retirement and happiness. By Tim Stobbs - an engineer in his late thirties with two kids.

feeds.title: Retired At 48
feeds.description: We are an active, professional couple who retired from our careers at age 48 and wrote a book about our experiences. Retired at 48 is about one couple's journey to a pensionless retirement.

feeds.title: Minafi Blog
feeds.description: Reach financial independence early through investing, minimalism & mindfulness. I help millennials invest to reach their financial goals quickly and easily.

feeds.title: Get Rich Slowly
feeds.description: Get Rich Slowly is a site for anyone who craves greater financial freedom. I'll share tips for digging out of debt and building a better financial future. I'll teach you how to do stock-market investing without gambling or excessive risk. I'm not going to give you a hard sell on any products or books. What you will find at Get Rich Slowly is daily information about personal finance and related topics.

feeds.title: Eat Sleep Breathe FI
feeds.description: Hi, I'm Chrissy and I'm a FI fanatic! Join me as I share how we're reaching FI in our 40s, with kids, on one income, in high-cost Vancouver.

feeds.title: Journey To Launch Blog
feeds.description: Journey to Launch emerged in 2016 by founder Jamila Souffrant initially as one person's expedition to reach financial independence. Our mission here at Journey to Launch is to help you eliminate debt, save more money and increase your net worth so that you can ultimately achieve Financial Freedom & Independence.

feeds.title: One Frugal Girl » Financial Independence
feeds.description: Hi, I'm Jewels, otherwise known as One Frugal Girl. I am a forty-year-old wife, mother, blogger, personal finance enthusiast, optimist, former software developer, and achiever of financial independence. This blog is my story. Welcome to my little corner of the Internet.

feeds.title: Leisure Freak Blog
feeds.description: Leisure Freak, Retire Early and Often through Frugal Living is a site dedicated to those who are truly passionate about retiring early & living their dream lifestyle.

feeds.title: Early Retirement Extreme
feeds.description: Learn how to become financially independent through frugality, self-sufficiency, sustainable behavior, investing, DIY ethics and voluntary simplicity! Jacob became financially independent at 30 and retired at 33 and he writes a blog about how to retire extremely early.

feeds.title: Root of Good
feeds.description: Covers blog posts on retirement, financial independence, parenting, personal finance, investing, money hacks, travel, DIY and lifestyle. Root of Good tells how the author managed to accumulate enough wealth to make him financially independent which allowed him to retire at age 33.

feeds.title: Our Rich Journey Blog
feeds.description: We're Amon & Christina. We're former federal government employees that focused on saving, making, and investing money so that we could grow enough wealth in our investments to never have to work again. So, if you're interested in learning how to save, make and invest money on the road to financial independence and retiring early - this site is for you!
